PS5 DualSense Controller Test: Buttons, Sticks & Triggers

By PadLab · Updated October 5, 2026 · 4 minute read

Use PadLab to inspect the inputs your PS5 DualSense or DualSense Edge exposes to the browser. This is a quick button, stick, trigger and connection check—not a firmware calibration utility.

Run a DualSense test

  1. Connect with a USB data cable or pair through Bluetooth.
  2. Open the PadLab tester and press a button while the page is focused.
  3. Press Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, the D-pad, bumpers, Options, Share and both stick clicks.
  4. Squeeze L2 and R2 gradually, then release both sticks and run the drift sample.

What PadLab can see

PadLab can display browser-exposed buttons, axes, standard mapping and supported vibration. DualSense-specific features such as adaptive trigger resistance, touchpad gestures, light-bar state, microphone status and every advanced haptic mode may not be exposed through the standard Gamepad API.

DualSense drift and center offset

Leave both sticks untouched and use the three-second drift test. Review mean and peak radial offset, then compare that observation with the deadzone used by your game. A small nonzero center value is not a universal failure threshold.

Read how stick drift and deadzones work.

If the controller is missing

Use a known data cable, keep the page visible, press a physical button, and check whether the controller is connected to another device. See controller detection troubleshooting.
